name: Agents
oneLiner: Systems that pursue a goal over many steps: plan, act with tools, check the result, repeat.

analogy.text: A new employee given a goal instead of a script: they work out the steps, use the office tools and check their own work.
analogy.breaks: An employee builds judgement over months. An agent's 'experience' is only what fits in its context and memory, and it can repeat a mistake confidently.

examples: Agent harnesses (Claude Code, OpenCode, OpenClaw, Hermes Agent)
givesAbove: Completed multi-step tasks, not just single answers.
needsBelow: Tools, retrieval and model calls arranged by Orchestration & Tooling.

walkthrough.title: A goal, not a script
walkthrough.text: Someone asks: “fix the failing login test”. The agent loop starts: read the code, choose a step, act, look at the result, repeat.

walkthrough.title: The harness keeps it safe
walkthrough.text: The harness runs each tool call, asks before risky commands, and trims the context so the long task still fits.

walkthrough.title: A coding agent does the work
walkthrough.text: Inside the harness, a coding agent edits two files and reruns the tests until they pass.

walkthrough.title: Checking the real page
walkthrough.text: To be sure, it opens the login page in a browser, takes screenshots and clicks through it, like a person would.

walkthrough.title: Splitting the job
walkthrough.text: For a bigger change, a lead agent hands tests and review to sub-agents, each running its own loop.
